text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Civil Servants Trade Union legal advisor, Viva Nyimba, said the union and not government should pay striking workers' wages for the period they are on strike, now in its third week.
- Presidential aide Ken Lipenga is to contest the by-election in Mulanje which became vacant this year after its member of parliament died.
- The Customs Workers Union has declared it will join the nation-wide civil servant's strike after government apparently interdicted more than 200 strikers.
- The Electoral Commission spent more than two million kwacha in a Blantyre by-election.
